title: Two Sum
prompt: Return the indices of the two numbers in nums that add up to target.

segments.text: Two Sum. The classic warm-up in almost every Python interview.

The brute force is two nested loops, but we can do it in one pass. We walk the list once and keep a dictionary that maps each value to its index. For every number we work out what we still need to reach the target. If that complement is already in the dictionary, we've found our pair, so we return both indices.
Run it on a quick example and we get the two indices back.

segments.question: Why store each number only after checking for its complement?
segments.answer: So an element can never pair with itself.

segments.text: One pass, linear time. Trading a little memory for speed is the whole trick.
